claims.text: An AIRPORT pickup requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of 480 seconds, and the driver's own trace credits him with 255 seconds — a single run of five qualifying fixes from 23:42:21 to 23:46:36 inside the 150 m radius for this zone class. That is a shortfall of 225 seconds. POL-NS-06 makes the cancellation fee unchargeable where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum for the zone class, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages, and the $6.00 must be refunded in full. The trace is impaired at policy level under POL-NS-08(b) — 22.8% coverage, a 52 second sample interval against a 10 second expected cadence, and gaps of 175 and 186 seconds inside the trip — and I disclose that impairment; the shortfall survives the discount because this is the longest qualifying run the record contains and the driver's own trip record independently reports a 6.9 minute wait.

Even if the driver were credited with every single second from the first qualifying in-geofence fix to the moment he cancelled, he still cannot reach 480 seconds. POL-NS-01 limb (c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' tap, and 23:42:21 to the cancellation at 23:49:05 is 404 seconds — 76 seconds short. Neither the 186 second gap that ends at the first fix nor the unfixed tail from the last fix at 23:46:36 to the cancellation can close that gap, because the clause's clock starts no earlier than the trace's own first qualifying fix and stops at the driver's own cancellation. Nothing here requires me to interpolate: the bound is drawn from a derived timestamp in EV-GPS-00210 and the cancellation timestamp in EV-TRIP-00210.

POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (d) fails on its own, independently of how the dwell is measured. Limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed. The trip record shows termination at 23:49:05 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW; the required 480 seconds had not elapsed — measured from his own 'arrived' marker at 23:42:10 they ran out at 23:50:10, and measured as the clause directs from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 23:42:21 they ran out at 23:50:21. A cancellation 65 to 76 seconds early is not a termination at or after the elapse of the minimum dwell, so the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 at all.

The driver's statement that he was at T1 arrival Door 6 'for more than eight minutes' is contradicted by his own device and by his own trip record. The trace holds five qualifying fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT radius across a 255 second run, and the trip record itself reports a 6.9 minute wait — under eight minutes even on the platform's own arrival-tap clock, which is not the clock limb (c) uses. The bundle contains no artifact that corroborates his assertion, and it contains his own telemetry against it.

Satisfying the arrival test does not save the fee, and the driver should not be heard to argue otherwise. POL-NS-02 deems the driver to have arrived where at least three consecutive accurate fixes fall within the radius, and it says in terms that where qualifying in-radius fixes exist 'this clause is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01 limb (c)'. Here arrival is verified and the dwell is 255 seconds against a 480 second minimum, so limb (b) is met, limb (c) is not, and the conjunctive test in POL-NS-01 still fails.

The rider's account that he was standing at Door 6 the whole time is not rebutted by this trace, because the trace carries no rider track at all: rider_fix_count is 0 and rider_presence reports available false. POL-NS-04 limb (c) makes an absent rider track UNDECIDABLE and neutral — neither satisfied nor failed — and the rider's presence may not be inferred away from it. I disclose that the omission is itself a defect of the trace under POL-NS-08(b); under POL-GEN-02 an impaired artifact may still be argued on its merits, and here the omission leaves rider presence unproven rather than disproven, which is not the driver's point to win.

The chat record does not show this rider silent or uncooperative. The log contains no driver message of any kind and no reply; trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so POL-NS-04 limb (b) is satisfied on the face of the record. The log is impaired under POL-NS-08(c) — it holds 2 messages against a recorded chat_message_count of 4, its msg_ids run 001 then 004, and it is flagged truncated — so two messages are missing from the very window in issue, and limb (a) cannot be affirmatively denied against the rider on a log that is missing its own messages.

The rider was engaged with the app at the pickup point, not absent from it: he read the system message 'Your driver has arrived' at 23:42:30, nineteen seconds after it was sent at 23:42:11, and he messaged the driver at 23:49:40, thirty-five seconds after the cancellation at 23:49:05, asking why the trip was cancelled and stating he was at Door 6. That is the conduct of a rider waiting at the kerb for a car he could not see, and it is the only rider-side record the driver's own truncated log leaves standing.

The driver cannot top his 255 seconds up to the 480 second minimum. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory that is present and populated, and whose type is KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, covers the pickup road and the waiting period. EV-ADVIS-00210-01 is MISSING with no payload and carries weight 0.0, and the derived computation records run_count 0, so there is not even a second in-geofence interval to add to the first. The absence of an advisory is itself citable, but it exonerates no one, and the shortfall stands unmodified.

No driver compensation is payable on this record. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 states that where the cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The remedy that follows from this trip's own numbers is the return of the contested $6.00 to the rider, not a payment to the driver out of it.

The disputed $6.00 is still PENDING and refund_issued_sgd stands at 0.00, so NO_ACTION would leave the rider carrying the whole contested charge; the rider is the filing party, so only a refund leaves him not carrying it. And if any part of the deciding fact is held to rest on the trace impaired under POL-NS-08(b), then at the very least the fee must be held rather than collected while the case is reviewed — it must not be taken from the rider in the meantime.

claims.text: Limb (a) of the baseline no-show test is met on the face of the platform's own trip record: TRP-00210 carries a driver 'arrived' event stamped 2026-08-01T23:42:10+08:00, and that event is corroborated to the second by the SYSTEM message 'Your driver has arrived' pushed at 23:42:11.

Limb (d) is met: the trip was terminated by the driver at 23:49:05 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - one of the three codes limb (d) recognises - the status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER, started_at is null, and no boarding event is recorded anywhere in the trip record.

Limb (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are met on the driver's own trace: his minimum distance to the pickup pin is 96.01 m against a 150 m arrival radius for the AIRPORT zone class, and the trace carries 5 consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes. POL-NS-02 says in terms that where qualifying in-radius fixes exist the clause is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01 limb (c) - which is exactly where the driver side argues this case.

The 'arrived' marker at 23:42:10 sits inside a 186-second sampling gap running 23:39:15 to 23:42:21, and the very next fix, 11 seconds later, already places the driver inside the 150 m radius. There is no clock-skew defect here: the marker and the nearest fix are 11 seconds apart, far inside the 90-second limb of POL-NS-08(a), so the arrival event and the GPS record are safely matched.

The rider was told the driver had arrived. The system notification was delivered at 23:42:11 and the rider read it at 23:42:30; she then sent nothing for seven minutes, her only message on the log ('why cancel?? i was at door 6') arriving at 23:49:40, thirty-five seconds after the driver had already cancelled. I disclose that EV-CHAT-00210 is impaired under POL-NS-08(c): it holds 2 messages against the 4 that trip_record.chat_message_count records for this trip, so two messages are not before the tribunal.

The driver's GPS trace is impaired under POL-NS-08(b) and any dwell figure taken from it must be disclosed as impaired. Coverage is 22.8 per cent; the sample interval is 52 seconds against an expected 10; the trace holds only 9 fixes in total; it contains gaps of 175 seconds and 186 seconds, both beyond the 120-second threshold; it carries only 5 fixes across the 23:42:10-23:49:05 waiting window, fewer than the 6 that limb (b) requires; and its final fix at 23:46:36 leaves the last 149 seconds before cancellation completely unobserved.

The longest qualifying in-geofence run reads 255 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, but that figure is bounded by the fixes the trace happens to carry rather than by the driver's actual conduct: he is unobserved across the 186-second gap that straddles the arrival marker and unobserved for the final 149 seconds before he cancelled. On this cadence the 255-second reading is a floor, not a measurement, and it cannot affirmatively establish a shortfall below the minimum.

The shortfall the rider needs under POL-NS-06 is carried by one artifact, and that artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b). POL-NS-08 provides that a claim resting on an impaired artifact cannot alone support a ruling against the party it disfavours, and its closing sentence caps the ruling at PARTIAL_REFUND and sends the case to review under POL-NS-09 where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired. A full refund under POL-NS-06 is therefore not available to the rider on this record, and the disputed fee should be held rather than handed back.

POL-NS-04 cannot be run for the rider. Its limb (c) needs a rider_track, and this trace carries none - the rider_presence block is marked unavailable - so rider presence is undecidable and, by the clause's own words, neutral rather than adverse. The clause requires all three limbs to hold before it exonerates anyone, and limb (c) cannot hold, so no refund flows from POL-NS-04 whatever view is taken of the chat.

POL-NS-05 does not fire either. That clause needs a GPS fix matched to the arrival timestamp showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above, and there is no fix at 23:42:10 at all - the marker falls inside the 23:39:15 to 23:42:21 gap, whose longest single interval is 186 seconds. There is no admissible basis on which to call this a false arrival marker, so the waiting clock is not recomputed and the fee is not voided on this route.

This dispute is rider-filed, the SGD 6.00 charge is still PENDING on the ledger and SGD 0.00 has been refunded. Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION is party-relative: it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, so on this file declining to disturb the charge is a real disposition that preserves the driver's fee, not a nullity.

Nothing in the driver's profile withholds his compensation. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check requires BOTH limbs, and neither is met: no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause demands, and 2 divided by 156 completed trips in 30 days is 0.013, well under the 0.08 rate limb. I cite only those two profile fields, as POL-GEN-01 permits for this test.

The money on the ledger is internally clean, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect to discount: the cancellation fee of SGD 6.00 equals the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), which is the result fee_schedule.resolution_rule prescribes. On the 80 per cent rate the driver's compensation on this charge is SGD 4.80 of the SGD 6.00.

Neither abuse escalation trigger on the parties' histories is met: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) requires, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, below the 2 that POL-NS-09(c) requires. Nothing in the profiles takes this case out of an ordinary monetary disposition, so the impairment point above, not the parties' records, is the only matter that could send it to review.

ruling.explanation:
Decision: the $6.00 no-show fee is refunded to the rider in full. This is the reasoning for both of you.

THE FEE IS NOT CHARGEABLE. An airport no-show fee requires the driver to hold position inside the Terminal 1 pickup geofence for a continuous 480 seconds, timed from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the 'arrived' tap (POL-NS-01(c)). The driver's own trace shows his longest qualifying in-geofence run at 255 seconds — five fixes from 23:42:21 to 23:46:36 inside the 150 m airport radius — a 225-second shortfall against the 480-second minimum, so the fee fails under POL-NS-06. Even on the most generous reading the driver himself could offer, his 'arrived' tap at 23:42:10 and his cancellation at 23:49:05 span only 415 seconds (6.9 minutes, the figure his own trip record carries), still short of 480. Nothing tops the dwell up: POL-NS-06(i) allows separate in-geofence intervals to be added only where a present, populated traffic advisory of a qualifying type covers the pickup road, and EV-ADVIS-00210-01 is MISSING with no payload (weight 0.0), and the trace shows no second in-geofence interval to add (run_count 0).

EVIDENCE QUALITY, stated plainly as the rules require. The driver's GPS trace EV-GPS-00210 is impaired under POL-NS-08(b): it holds only 5 fixes across the waiting window where 6 are required, at 22.8% coverage and a 52-second cadence against the 10-second expected cadence, with a 186-second gap straddling the arrival marker and no rider track. Its 255-second figure is down-weighted for that reason and could not on its own carry a ruling against the driver. It is not the only record of the wait, however. The trip record EV-TRIP-00210 is clean — the clock-skew limb POL-NS-08(a) does not fire, its arrival marker sitting 11 seconds from the nearest GPS fix — and it independently records the same window, arrival 23:42:10 to cancellation 23:49:05 with a 6.9-minute wait, under the 8-minute minimum. The shortfall therefore does not rest on the impaired trace alone, and the sole-evidence escalation in POL-NS-08 and POL-NS-09(e) is not engaged. The chat log EV-CHAT-00210 is impaired under POL-NS-08(c) (2 messages against the 4 the trip record records; msg_ids 001 and 004; truncated), but it goes only to fault allocation under POL-NS-03, which does not arise here, and not to the refund.

POINTS RAISED ON BOTH SIDES. The driver's statement that he waited 'more than eight minutes' is unsupported by any artifact and is contradicted by his own device and his own trip record. Arrival under POL-NS-02 is verified but does not save the fee: that clause sends the dispute to the dwell test, which fails. The driver's limbs (a), (b) and (d) are accepted and still immaterial, because POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (c) fails. POL-NS-05 is not reached — no fix coincides with the 23:42:10 marker, which falls inside the 186-second gap — so no false-arrival finding is made and no false-arrival referral issues. POL-NS-04 cannot be run for want of a rider track; its rider-presence limb is undecidable and neutral, and nothing is inferred from it either way.

DRIVER COMPENSATION. None is payable: POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 states that no compensation is payable on a shortfall. The anti-farming check would not have tripped in any event — 2 no-show terminations against 156 completed trips, a rate of 0.013, both below the clause's thresholds. No abuse escalation arises either: 1 rider no-show dispute in 30 days (below 3) and 0 counterparty disputes in 90 days for either party (below 2).

THE MONEY. The $6.00 charged equals the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), which is what fee_schedule.resolution_rule prescribes, so there is no fare-integrity defect under POL-NS-08(d). The cancellation-fee line is the whole charge (base fare, distance fare, time fare, platform fee and airport surcharge are all 0.00). $6.00 is returned to the rider; the charge is not left standing.

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer, and the disputed SGD 6.00 cancellation fee is held — not collected from the rider and not refunded — until that review is finished.

The fee turns on one fact: whether the driver held position inside the 150 m Changi Terminal 1 pickup geofence for a continuous 480 seconds (480 s is the AIRPORT minimum under POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-06). The driver's own trace, EV-GPS-00210, records his longest qualifying in-geofence run as 255 seconds, from 23:42:21 to 23:46:36. Even crediting him with every second from that first in-geofence fix to his cancellation at 23:49:05 (EV-TRIP-00210) gives 404 seconds — 76 seconds short. But that trace is impaired and it is the only evidence of the dwell. It holds just 5 fixes across the waiting window, below the 6 POL-NS-08(b) requires; it carries gaps of 175 s and 186 s, over the 120 s threshold; coverage is 22.8% against a 52 s cadence and a 10 s expected interval; and it contains no rider track at all. The 186 s gap (23:39:15 to 23:42:21) straddles the arrival marker, so the driver's entry into the geofence is not observed, and the last 149 seconds before cancellation are unobserved too. His entry could therefore have been earlier than 23:42:21, which makes the 404-second figure not a safe upper bound, and equally his hold could have ended before 23:49:05. I cannot find that the driver waited 480 seconds, and I cannot find that he did not. An undecided limb supports neither the fee (POL-NS-01) nor the refund (POL-NS-06). Because the sole evidence of the deciding fact is impaired, POL-NS-08's closing sentence and POL-NS-09(e) send the case to review and the fee is held. My confidence is 0.55, below the platform's 0.70 floor, which is a second escalation trigger under POL-NS-09(a).

On the rider's claims: the POL-NS-06 full-refund claim is rejected for the reason above — the 404-second bound assumes the recorded first fix is the true first, and the 186 s gap makes that assumption unsafe; the POL-NS-04 claim is accepted (the trace holds no rider track, so rider presence is undecidable and neutral — it neither proves nor disproves that the rider was at Door 6, and it is not a ground for a refund); the limb (d) argument is not reached, because whether the driver cancelled before the dwell elapsed depends on a dwell that is undecided; and the rider's fallback that the fee must at least be held rather than taken is the outcome I have reached.

On the driver's claims: the POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION claim is rejected — NO_ACTION would leave the SGD 6.00 standing, and the impaired record cannot support that; the POL-NS-07 compensation claim (SGD 4.80) is rejected because POL-NS-01 is not affirmatively satisfied and no compensation is payable while the fee is undecided; and the anti-farming check is in any event clean (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 156 completed trips, a rate of 0.013, against the clause's 4 and 0.08). The driver's statement that he waited 'more than eight minutes' is not corroborated and is contradicted by his own telemetry: the trip record itself reports a 6.9-minute wait (415 s, tap to cancellation), itself under eight minutes. No clock-skew defect is found (the arrival marker is 11 s from the nearest fix).

Other evidence: the chat log EV-CHAT-00210 is impaired under POL-NS-08(c) — it holds 2 messages against the 4 the trip record records and its ids run 001 then 004 — so the rider's 23:49:40 message ('why cancel?? i was at door 6') cannot by itself settle fault, and it does not change the outcome. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00210-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0), so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to add any second in-geofence interval — none exists in any case. The fare line is clean: SGD 6.00 equals the greater of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00), so no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect arises. Neither party's record raises an abuse trigger (rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1; both counterparty-dispute counts are 0).

Specific question for the reviewer: was the driver continuously inside the 150 m geofence for 480 seconds between 23:42 and 23:49 — did he enter before 23:42:21, and did he leave before 23:49:05 — and, if the missing chat messages can be recovered, did either party name a sub-location at Door 6 (which would bear on fault under POL-NS-03)?

To the rider and the driver: this case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves now — the $6.00 cancellation fee is placed on hold, neither collected from the rider nor refunded, while the review is pending. The fee is $6.00 because the AIRPORT zone-class fee ($6.00) is the greater of the two figures the fee schedule prescribes against the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), and that is the amount on the fare breakdown.

The charge stands or falls on POL-NS-01, which the driver must satisfy in full. Three limbs are met and I accept them: (a) an 'arrived' event at 23:42:10; (b) the driver's trace carries five qualifying fixes inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius, so arrival is deemed under POL-NS-02 — the marker is 11 seconds from the next fix, well inside the 90-second skew tolerance, so the match is safe; and (d) the driver terminated at 23:49:05 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the codes limb (d) recognises. Limb (c) — a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 480 seconds (8 minutes) for an AIRPORT pickup — cannot be decided on this record.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the disputed SGD 6.00 no-show fee is refunded to the rider in full.

Why the fee cannot stand. Under POL-NS-01 the fee is chargeable only if all four limbs hold, and limb (c) requires the driver to have held position inside the pickup geofence for a continuous dwell of at least 480 seconds at an AIRPORT pickup (fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec), measured from his first qualifying in-geofence fix and NOT from his 'arrived' tap. The driver did not. The platform's own trip record (EV-TRIP-00210) records his arrival event at 23:42:10 and his driver-terminated cancellation at 23:49:05 with reason RIDER_NO_SHOW - 415 seconds, 65 seconds short of 480, and its own wait-time figure of 6.9 minutes confirms it. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00210) agrees and is shorter on every reading: the longest continuous qualifying in-geofence run is 255 seconds (23:42:21 to 23:46:36, five qualifying fixes), and the span from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 23:42:21 to the cancellation at 23:49:05 is 404 seconds. Because limb (c) fails, the fee is not chargeable and POL-NS-06 refunds it in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

On the impairment point the driver raises. The GPS trace is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08(b): coverage 22.8%, a 52-second sample interval against an expected 10-second cadence, gaps of 175 and 186 seconds, only 5 fixes across the waiting window (fewer than the 6 the limb requires), and no rider track at all. I have named that impairment and its effect. It does not, however, carry the shortfall alone. The shortfall is carried independently by the trip record, a platform-generated artifact whose own arrival and cancellation timestamps bound the maximum possible dwell at 415 seconds even before the clause's later starting point is applied. The sole-evidence sentence of POL-NS-08 and the escalation trigger of POL-NS-09(e) are therefore not engaged, and this case is decided on its merits rather than sent to review.

The driver's arguments, answered. (1) His statement that he was at Door 6 'for more than eight minutes' is contradicted by his own device and by his own trip record, and no artifact supports the eight-minute claim; the driver says he does not know what to tell us, and his telemetry answers it. (2) His argument that the 255-second reading is a floor rather than a measurement because of the trace's gaps is rejected: the trip record's own arrival-to-cancellation span of 415 seconds caps the possible dwell regardless of any gap. (3) His argument that a full refund is unavailable and the fee should merely be held is rejected for the reason above - the deciding fact does not rest on the impaired trace alone. (4) Limb (a) (arrival event present) and limb (b)/POL-NS-02 proximity (minimum distance 96.01 m inside the 150 m AIRPORT radius, five consecutive qualifying fixes) are accepted; they do not save the fee because limb (c) still fails. (5) His point that limb (d)'s reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three recognised codes is accepted, but limb (d) also requires termination at or after the dwell elapsed, and the dwell never elapsed; in any event the fee fails on limb (c). (6) That the 23:42:10 marker sits inside the 186-second gap with the next fix 11 seconds away, so there is no POL-NS-08(a) clock-skew defect, is accepted. (7) That POL-NS-05 does not fire is accepted - there is no GPS fix at the arrival timestamp (it falls inside the 23:39:15-23:42:21 gap), so no false-arrival marker is established and no POL-NS-05(ii) referral is recorded. (8) That the anti-farming check does not trip (2 no-show terminations in 30 days against 156 completed trips, below both the count and rate thresholds) is accepted, citing only the two fields POL-GEN-01 permits for POL-NS-07. (9) That the ledger is internally clean under POL-NS-08(d) is accepted - the SGD 6.00 fee equals the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under fee_schedule.resolution_rule - but the driver's compensation of SGD 4.80 is not payable, because POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and POL-NS-06 states that where the dwell falls short the full refund stands and no compensation is payable. (10) That no POL-NS-09(c) or (d) abuse trigger fires is accepted.

The rider's other points, answered. His rider-presence argument is accepted as far as it goes: the trace carries no rider track, so POL-NS-04 limb (c) is undecidable and neutral and rider presence is neither proved nor disproved; POL-NS-04 therefore does not exonerate him and does not need to, because the refund follows from the dwell shortfall alone. His observation that the chat log is truncated (2 messages against the recorded chat_message_count of 4, msg_ids running 001 then 004) is accepted; it means the driver neither replied nor called within 120 seconds so far as the log shows, but nothing turns on rider conduct here. His point that the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00210-01, no payload) cannot permit separate in-geofence intervals to be summed under POL-NS-06(i) is accepted - there is no second interval and no qualifying advisory, so the 255-second reading cannot be topped up.

Amount. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00210) itemises the cancellation fee at SGD 6.00, still PENDING, with SGD 0.00 refunded. The full SGD 6.00 is returned to the rider. No driver compensation is payable and no referral is produced by any clause.

Confidence 0.85: the deciding shortfall rests on the platform's trip record, with the impaired GPS trace corroborating it and no material fact resting on an impaired artifact alone.

Coverage is 22.8 per cent; the sample interval is 52 seconds against an expected 10; the trace holds only 9 fixes in total; it contains gaps of 175 seconds and 186 seconds, both beyond the 120-second threshold; it carries only 5 fixes across the 23:42:10-23:49:05 waiting window, fewer than the 6 that limb (b) requires; and its final fix at 23:46:36 leaves the last 149 seconds before cancellation completely unobserved.

The longest qualifying in-geofence run reads 255 seconds against the 480-second AIRPORT minimum, but that figure is bounded by the fixes the trace happens to carry rather than by the driver's actual conduct: he is unobserved across the 186-second gap that straddles the arrival marker and unobserved for the final 149 seconds before he cancelled. On this cadence the 255-second reading is a floor, not a measurement, and it cannot affirmatively establish a shortfall below the minimum.

The shortfall the rider needs under POL-NS-06 is carried by one artifact, and that artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(b). POL-NS-08 provides that a claim resting on an impaired artifact cannot alone support a ruling against the party it disfavours, and its closing sentence caps the ruling at PARTIAL_REFUND and sends the case to review under POL-NS-09 where the sole evidence for the deciding fact is impaired. A full refund under POL-NS-06 is therefore not available to the rider on this record, and the disputed fee should be held rather than handed back.

POL-NS-04 cannot be run for the rider. Its limb (c) needs a rider_track, and this trace carries none - the rider_presence block is marked unavailable - so rider presence is undecidable and, by the clause's own words, neutral rather than adverse. The clause requires all three limbs to hold before it exonerates anyone, and limb (c) cannot hold, so no refund flows from POL-NS-04 whatever view is taken of the chat.

POL-NS-05 does not fire either. That clause needs a GPS fix matched to the arrival timestamp showing the driver more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above, and there is no fix at 23:42:10 at all - the marker falls inside the 23:39:15 to 23:42:21 gap, whose longest single interval is 186 seconds. There is no admissible basis on which to call this a false arrival marker, so the waiting clock is not recomputed and the fee is not voided on this route.
